results.bestEvidenceQuote: The project is eligible under the VCS Program REDD activity category of avoiding planned deforestation as per Appendix 1 of the VCS standard v5.0. The project area qualifies as forest and has remained forested for more than 10 years prior to the project start date, meeting the applicable forest definition thresholds. In the absence of the project, the area was legally authorized and documented for conversion to non-forest land, which would have resulted in significant loss of forest carbon stocks. The project activities prevent this planned conversion by maintaining the forest cover and protecting existing carbon stocks, thereby reducing net GHG emissions associated with deforestation.

Project Crediting Period and Registration Timelines 3.8.1 The initial crediting period start date shall: 1) be consistent with the definition of initial crediting period start date in the VCS Program Definitions. 2) conform to any criteria set out in the applied methodology. 3) be established based on implementation of the earliest project activity, where the project includes multiple project activities. 4) determine the start of the first project monitoring period, which shall begin on the initial crediting period start date. Some methodologies may require project proponents to quantify emissions that occur prior to this date to account for all project or baseline emissions. The initial crediting period start date for the Marcondes REDD+ Project is 01 May 2023, which is consistent with the definition of the initial crediting period start date under the VCS Program and conforms to the criteria specified in the applied methodology. The project does not involve multiple project activities and implements a single REDD+ activity in a grouped project design aimed at avoiding planned deforestation (APD). Accordingly, the crediting period start date is established based on the earliest implementation of project activities undertaken to prevent planned deforestation. The selected date corresponds to the commencement of project implementation activities, including the execution of carbon credit agreements with participating landowners and the initiation of monitoring activities across properties located in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha in the state of Amazonas. This date also determines the start of the first monitoring period, from which emission reductions are accounted for under the project. The applied methodology does not require quantification of emissions occurring prior to the crediting period start date; therefore, this provision is not applicable to the project. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 4 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 1 SUMMARY OF PROJECT BENEFITS The Marcondes Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) Project is an AFOLU initiative focused on Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), spanning a total area of 74,783 hectares of Amazon rainforest across 36 rural properties in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project's core objective is to conserve approximately 14,957 hectares of dense ombrophilous forest that would otherwise be legally converted to cattle pasture under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). By the end of the 40-year crediting period, an estimated 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of net GHG emission reductions will be achieved. This project is developed in alignment with the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity (CCB) Standards v3.1, ensuring measurable benefits across three critical areas. From a climate perspective, the conservation of 74,783 hectares of standing forest maintains critical carbon stocks (668.42 tCO₂e/ha) and preserves the hydrological functions of the Nhamundá River basin, a clearwater tributary draining the southern Guiana Shield. For local communities, the project delivers transformative benefits to the Comunidade Tradicional São Tomé do Mocambo do Arari (~80 families, Parintins) through a formal Benefit- Sharing Plan encompassing direct monetary benefits (participation in carbon credit revenue), community infrastructure (sanitation, energy, communication), training and capacity building, participatory forest monitoring with paid community guards, and cultural heritage support for traditional artisanal ceramics. The 40%/60% benefit-sharing structure ensures 60% of carbon revenues flow directly to the 36 participating landowners. The project prioritizes biodiversity conservation within the Uatumã–Trombetas Moist Forests ecoregion, harboring at least 10 globally threatened mammal species (including Inia geoffrensis — EN, Pteronura brasiliensis — EN, Tapirus terrestris — VU), 250+ bird species, 300+ fish species (including endemic taxa in the Nhamundá River), and threatened tree species (Swietenia macrophylla — VU, Bertholletia excelsa — VU). Forest conservation preserves ecosystem functions including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, watershed protection, and ecological connectivity. 1.1 Unique Project Benefits Outcome or impact estimated by the end of project lifetime Section referenc e 1) Avoiding the emission of 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of GHG, contributing to climate change mitigation over a 40-year period. 2.1.13 & 3

The project area lies within the Middle Amazon basin, in the Nhamundá River watershed, a region of significant ecological value facing persistent deforestation pressures. According to Global Forest Watch (2020), Nhamundá municipality retains approximately 1.26 million hectares of natural forest, covering roughly 89% of its land area. Despite recent national progress, PRODES/INPE data shows Amazon deforestation declined by 50% cumulatively between 2022 and 2025, reaching 5,796 km² in the August 2024– July 2025 period the state of Amazonas remains the second-largest contributor to absolute deforestation in the Legal Amazon, with 1,016 km² cleared in the most recent PRODES cycle. The main drivers of deforestation in the project region include legal land clearance for cattle ranching and agriculture, selective and illegal logging, and pressure from infrastructure development and land speculation along river corridors. Federal Legislation ▪ Brazilian Civil Code (Law No. 10.406/2002, Articles 1.196–1.228): Recognizes possession (posse) as a protected right and establishes usucapião as a legal pathway to ownership. ▪ Brazilian Forest Code (Law No. 12.651/2012): Establishes the requirement for Cadastro Ambiental Rural (CAR) registration and mandates an 80% Legal Reserve for rural properties located in the Legal Amazon. ▪ Law No. 10.267/2001 and Decree No. 4.449/2002: Establish the SIGEF system (Sistema de Gestão Fundiária) and define requirements for georeferenced rural property registration. ▪ Law No. 6.015/1973 (Public Registries Law): Regulates property registration and the Matrícula system at the Cartório de Registro de Imóveis. State Legislation (Amazonas) ▪ State Law No. 2.665/2001: Regulates state land policy, including the issuance of Concessão de Direito Real de Uso (CDRU) for state lands and terras devolutas. ▪ State Law No. 3.135/2007: Establishes the Amazonas State Policy on Climate Change, providing the legal framework for carbon credit projects and ecosystem services. Land Ownership The Marcondes REDD+ project is a grouped project and for validation comprises 36 rural properties located primarily in the municipality of Nhamundá, Parintins and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The total project area is approximately 74,698 hectares, held by approximately 24 landowners and legal entities. All 36 project properties are registered in the SIGEF system (Sistema de Gestão Fundiária) managed by INCRA, providing legally recognized, georeferenced, non-overlapping property boundaries. All properties are also registered in the Cadastro Ambiental Rural (CAR), which includes declared georeferenced boundaries, identification of Permanent Protection Areas (APPs), and demarcation of Legal Reserves in accordance with the 80% requirement applicable in the Legal Amazon. Applications for Concessão de Direito Real de Uso (CDRU) have been submitted to the SECT (Secretaria de Estado das Cidades e Territórios) for all properties, providing secure long-term rights of land use and management. Environmental license applications (Autorização de Supressão Vegetal — ASV) have been filed with IPAAM (Instituto de Proteção Ambiental do Amazonas) for all properties, confirming the legal authorization for land conversion that constitutes the basis for the APD baseline scenario. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 43 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 eastern Amazon where planned deforestation is legally permissible and widely practiced due to expanding pressures from cattle ranching, agriculture, timber extraction, and other land-use conversion activities. Without the project, these drivers would continue to advance, resulting in large-scale forest loss, degradation of ecosystems, and a decline in ecosystem services that sustain local communities. No government program, private organization, or community initiative currently possesses the financial, technical, or institutional capacity to prevent this deforestation or to generate the significant social and environmental benefits that the project will deliver. Although Brazilian environmental legislation primarily the Forest Code establishes requirements for Legal Reserves and Areas of Permanent Preservation, enforcement in remote Amazonian regions is limited. Environmental agencies such as IBAMA, ICMBio, and state-level authorities operate with insufficient personnel, financial resources, and field presence to monitor land-use change effectively. As a result, illegal deforestation persists, and legally authorized clearing continues unchecked. The project activities would not occur without carbon finance due to substantial financial barriers. Local communities lack the investment capacity needed to install renewable energy systems, develop potable water infrastructure, or establish agro-industries for processing NTFPs. Landowners similarly lack resources to implement forest monitoring systems, engage professional biodiversity technicians, or conduct long-term conservation planning. No government or donor program is currently committed to filling these gaps. Significant technological and knowledge barriers also prevent the implementation of sustainable development actions in the without-project scenario. Community members do not have access to the technical expertise required to manage NTFP value chains, apply sustainable harvesting techniques, conduct biodiversity monitoring, or maintain renewable energy systems. 2.2.4 Benefits to be used as Offsets (CCB, G2.2) The community and biodiversity benefits are not intended to be used as offsets but are documented and monitored under the CCB Standard to demonstrate the project's net positive impacts on local communities and ecosystems. 2.3 Safeguards and Stakeholder Engagement 2.3.1 Stakeholder Identification (VCS, 3.18, 3.19; CCB G1.5) The stakeholder identification process for the Marcondes REDD+ project was conducted using a structured, two-phase assessment, combining remote analysis and on-the-ground field validation. Stakeholders were identified based on their legal rights, forest resource dependence, potential influence on project outcomes, and possession of relevant local knowledge. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 10 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 2 PROJECT DETAILS 2.1 Project Goals, Design and Long-Term Viability 2.1.1 Summary Description of the Project (VCS, 3.2, 3.6, 3.10, 3.11, 3.13, 3.14; CCB, G1.2) The Marcondes REDD+ project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The project area lies within the Middle Amazon basin, in the Nhamundá River watershed, a region of significant ecological value facing persistent deforestation pressures. According to Global Forest Watch (2020), Nhamundá municipality retains approximately 1.26 million hectares of natural forest, covering roughly 89% of its land area. Despite recent national progress, PRODES/INPE data shows Amazon deforestation declined by 50% cumulatively between 2022 and 2025, reaching 5,796 km² in the August 2024– July 2025 period the state of Amazonas remains the second-largest contributor to absolute deforestation in the Legal Amazon, with 1,016 km² cleared in the most recent PRODES cycle. The main drivers of deforestation in the project region include legal land clearance for cattle ranching and agriculture, selective and illegal logging, and pressure from infrastructure development and land speculation along river corridors. The Marcondes REDD+ project aims to avoid planned deforestation and degradation across a total project area of approximately 74,783 hectares (per GIS measurement, SIRGAS 2000 – EPSG 4674), comprising 36 rural properties (fazendas) held by approximately 24 landowners and entities. As an Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) project under VM0007 v1.8, the project prevents the legally authorized conversion of 20% of each property's area (approximately 14,957 ha total APD area) from dense ombrophilous forest to cattle pasture. Under the baseline scenario, landowners would legally convert these forest areas to cattle pasture in accordance with the Brazilian Forest Code, resulting in significant carbon emissions from forest clearing and land-use change. The project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá (pop. 20,136, IBGE 2022; IDHM 0.586), Parintins (pop. 96,251), and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The total estimated emission reductions and removals (ERRs) generated during the crediting period are 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e. The project crediting period spans 40 years, from 01 May 2023 to 30 April 2063. During this period, the average annual ERRs are estimated at 250,212.95 tCO₂e per year. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 4 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 1 SUMMARY OF PROJECT BENEFITS The Marcondes Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) Project is an AFOLU initiative focused on Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), spanning a total area of 74,783 hectares of Amazon rainforest across 36 rural properties in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project's core objective is to conserve approximately 14,957 hectares of dense ombrophilous forest that would otherwise be legally converted to cattle pasture under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). By the end of the 40-year crediting period, an estimated 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of net GHG emission reductions will be achieved. This project is developed in alignment with the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity (CCB) Standards v3.1, ensuring measurable benefits across three critical areas. From a climate perspective, the conservation of 74,783 hectares of standing forest maintains critical carbon stocks (668.42 tCO₂e/ha) and preserves the hydrological functions of the Nhamundá River basin, a clearwater tributary draining the southern Guiana Shield. For local communities, the project delivers transformative benefits to the Comunidade Tradicional São Tomé do Mocambo do Arari (~80 families, Parintins) through a formal Benefit- Sharing Plan encompassing direct monetary benefits (participation in carbon credit revenue), community infrastructure (sanitation, energy, communication), training and capacity building, participatory forest monitoring with paid community guards, and cultural heritage support for traditional artisanal ceramics. The 40%/60% benefit-sharing structure ensures 60% of carbon revenues flow directly to the 36 participating landowners. The project prioritizes biodiversity conservation within the Uatumã–Trombetas Moist Forests ecoregion, harboring at least 10 globally threatened mammal species (including Inia geoffrensis — EN, Pteronura brasiliensis — EN, Tapirus terrestris — VU), 250+ bird species, 300+ fish species (including endemic taxa in the Nhamundá River), and threatened tree species (Swietenia macrophylla — VU, Bertholletia excelsa — VU). Forest conservation preserves ecosystem functions including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, watershed protection, and ecological connectivity. 1.1 Unique Project Benefits Outcome or impact estimated by the end of project lifetime Section referenc e 1) Avoiding the emission of 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of GHG, contributing to climate change mitigation over a 40-year period. 2.1.13 & 3

CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 4 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 1 SUMMARY OF PROJECT BENEFITS The Marcondes Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) Project is an AFOLU initiative focused on Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), spanning a total area of 74,783 hectares of Amazon rainforest across 36 rural properties in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project's core objective is to conserve approximately 14,957 hectares of dense ombrophilous forest that would otherwise be legally converted to cattle pasture under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). By the end of the 40-year crediting period, an estimated 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of net GHG emission reductions will be achieved. This project is developed in alignment with the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity (CCB) Standards v3.1, ensuring measurable benefits across three critical areas. From a climate perspective, the conservation of 74,783 hectares of standing forest maintains critical carbon stocks (668.42 tCO₂e/ha) and preserves the hydrological functions of the Nhamundá River basin, a clearwater tributary draining the southern Guiana Shield. For local communities, the project delivers transformative benefits to the Comunidade Tradicional São Tomé do Mocambo do Arari (~80 families, Parintins) through a formal Benefit- Sharing Plan encompassing direct monetary benefits (participation in carbon credit revenue), community infrastructure (sanitation, energy, communication), training and capacity building, participatory forest monitoring with paid community guards, and cultural heritage support for traditional artisanal ceramics. The 40%/60% benefit-sharing structure ensures 60% of carbon revenues flow directly to the 36 participating landowners. The project prioritizes biodiversity conservation within the Uatumã–Trombetas Moist Forests ecoregion, harboring at least 10 globally threatened mammal species (including Inia geoffrensis — EN, Pteronura brasiliensis — EN, Tapirus terrestris — VU), 250+ bird species, 300+ fish species (including endemic taxa in the Nhamundá River), and threatened tree species (Swietenia macrophylla — VU, Bertholletia excelsa — VU). Forest conservation preserves ecosystem functions including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, watershed protection, and ecological connectivity. 1.1 Unique Project Benefits Outcome or impact estimated by the end of project lifetime Section referenc e 1) Avoiding the emission of 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of GHG, contributing to climate change mitigation over a 40-year period. 2.1.13 & 3

CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 41 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 Permanence Mechanisms: ▪ 100-year longevity commitment in all carbon credit agreements ▪ VCS Standard v5.0, Section 3.2.19 provisions for instance exits ▪ AFOLU Non-Permanence Risk buffer pool ▪ Integration of sustainable economic activities (NTFP value chains, agroforestry) creating lasting conservation incentives 2.1.22 Financial Sustainability (CCB, G1.12) Financing of project activities is guaranteed by funds committed by the project proponents from the project start date until the first verification. The financing structure for the Marcondes REDD+ project is based on carbon credit revenues under the VCS Program, supplemented by initial investment from the project proponent: The Project Proponent has secured project financing through carbon credit offtaker agreements that provide advance funding for project implementation. A portion of the forecasted carbon credits has been committed under forward purchase agreements, ensuring financial resources are available from the project start date through the first verification cycle. This pre-financing covers monitoring infrastructure, community program implementation, and project development costs. Ongoing project financing is sustained through the sale of verified carbon credits (VCUs) on the voluntary carbon market, with revenues allocated according to the benefit-sharing structure defined in the carbon credit agreements with landowners. A portion of carbon credit revenues is dedicated to the community benefit fund, administered in consultation with the Comunidade São Tomé do Mocambo, ensuring long-term financial sustainability of community programs and biodiversity conservation activities. 2.2 Without-project Land Use Scenario and Additionality 2.2.1 Conditions Prior to Project Initiation and Land Use Scenarios without the Project (VCS, 3.13; CCB, G2.1) The following scenarios represent the range of possible land-use outcomes in the absence of the Marcondes REDD+ project. These scenarios were developed based on analysis of regional land- use dynamics, landowner intentions, legal frameworks, and historical deforestation patterns in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. SCENARIO 1: Maintenance of forest cover (conservation without project) Maintenance of the forest cover of 20% of the property, where land use conversion is allowed by law: the area is maintained without economic activities or conservation measures, but exposed to invasions and illegal deforestation, antecedents to livestock a common practice in the region. The landowner remains responsible for taxes to maintain ownership.

Forest Cover Maintenance and Monitoring The project maintains the Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) area approximately 14,940 hectares (20% of the total 74,698 ha project area) through continuous remote sensing (PRODES, DETER, and Planet imagery), drone surveillance, and ground patrols conducted in partnership with the Comunidade São Tomé do Mocambo. A monitoring protocol combining automated deforestation alerts with periodic field verification ensures early detection and response to any unauthorized clearing. Monitoring reports are produced quarterly and shared with landowners and community stakeholders. 2. Biodiversity Conservation and Research Biodiversity is conserved through habitat protection across the full 74,698 ha project area, monitoring of sensitive and threatened species including Harpy Eagle (Harpia harpyja, VU), Giant Otter (Pteronura brasiliensis, EN), Giant Armadillo (Priodontes maximus, VU), and Brazil Nut Tree (Bertholletia excelsa, VU), and support for scientific research. The project maintains permanent biodiversity monitoring plots and conducts annual fauna and flora surveys in collaboration with research institutions. Camera traps, acoustic monitoring, and participatory species inventories with community members complement systematic transect surveys. 3. Community Infrastructure and Livelihood Development The project enhances community well-being through targeted infrastructure investments and livelihood diversification programs. Specific interventions include: installation of solar energy systems for off-grid communities, provision of water filtration and treatment units, deployment of Starlink satellite internet systems for connectivity, and support for NTFP processing facilities (Brazil nut shelling, açaí processing, copaíba oil extraction). The project also supports community- based agroforestry initiatives, fair-trade certification for NTFP products, and market access development to diversify income sources beyond subsistence agriculture. 4. Capacity Building and Training Programs Training programs build skills in sustainable forest management, NTFP processing, fair trade, and renewable technologies, promoting gender and youth inclusion. The project is implemented through coordinated roles: Organica Consultoria LTDA oversees coordination, carbon accounting, and monitoring. The Comunidade São Tomé do Mocambo provides community liaison, local monitoring support, and stakeholder engagement. Urupolpas Comércio de Produtos Alimentícios Ltda serves as the local implementation partner for field operations, forest inventories, FPIC processes, and community relations. The technical team project provides expertise in forest engineering, GIS analysis, biodiversity assessment, and socioeconomic evaluation. The Theory of Change diagram will be developed as Appendix 2. Under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law No. 12.651/2012), rural properties in the Legal Amazon must maintain an 80% Legal Reserve, meaning up to 20% may be legally converted. SCENARIO 3: Illegal deforestation exceeding 20% Illegal deforestation of over 20% of the property (deforestation without a grant), where the conversion of land use exceeds the legal limit, driven by pasture expansion, agricultural purposes, or real estate speculation. Evidence of deforestation drivers in the project area includes: (a) all 36 property owners hold environmental license applications (ASV) filed with IPAAM, demonstrating documented intent to clear the legally convertible 20% of their properties for pasture establishment; (b) PRODES/INPE and MapBiomas historical data show progressive deforestation on comparable private properties in the Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha municipalities; (c) the Nhamundá municipal economy is dominated by cattle ranching and subsistence agriculture (IBGE Municipal Agricultural Production data), with limited economic alternatives; (d) pasture land/agriculture land values exceed forest land values in the region, providing direct economic incentive for conversion; (e) road access improvements and population growth (4.82% increase from 2022 to 2024 per IBGE) are increasing pressure on forested lands. 2.2.2 Most-Likely Scenario Justification (CCB, G2.1) The most likely scenario observed for the Marcondes project area is the conversion of land use and land cover from forest to livestock areas, legally (APD). Legal deforestation of 20% of the property (Scenario 2) is considered the most plausible baseline scenario because the land is expected to be converted to non-forest land and the conversion is legally authorized and documented, following VM0007 v1.8. The identified deforestation agents are the landowners themselves, who have documented legal authorization to clear up to 20% of their property areas under the Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). Evidence includes: (a) IPAAM environmental license applications (ASV) filed by all 36 property holders; (b) property registration in SIGEF demonstrating legal control of the land; (c) CAR (Cadastro Ambiental Rural) registration identifying the legal reserve and APD-eligible areas; (d) economic profile consistent with agricultural expansion the landowners include individual farmers, family groups (e.g., Fazenda AnaLina I/II/III, Fazenda Irmãos Marcondes, Fazenda André Marcondes IV/V), and corporate entities (FIEMU Corporation, Marcondes Q Corporation) whose primary economic activity is or would be cattle ranching. 2.2.3 Community and Biodiversity Additionality (CCB, G2.2) In the absence of the Marcondes REDD+ project, neither the community benefits nor the biodiversity conservation outcomes would occur. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 10 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 2 PROJECT DETAILS 2.1 Project Goals, Design and Long-Term Viability 2.1.1 Summary Description of the Project (VCS, 3.2, 3.6, 3.10, 3.11, 3.13, 3.14; CCB, G1.2) The Marcondes REDD+ project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The project area lies within the Middle Amazon basin, in the Nhamundá River watershed, a region of significant ecological value facing persistent deforestation pressures. According to Global Forest Watch (2020), Nhamundá municipality retains approximately 1.26 million hectares of natural forest, covering roughly 89% of its land area. Despite recent national progress, PRODES/INPE data shows Amazon deforestation declined by 50% cumulatively between 2022 and 2025, reaching 5,796 km² in the August 2024– July 2025 period the state of Amazonas remains the second-largest contributor to absolute deforestation in the Legal Amazon, with 1,016 km² cleared in the most recent PRODES cycle. The main drivers of deforestation in the project region include legal land clearance for cattle ranching and agriculture, selective and illegal logging, and pressure from infrastructure development and land speculation along river corridors. The Marcondes REDD+ project aims to avoid planned deforestation and degradation across a total project area of approximately 74,783 hectares (per GIS measurement, SIRGAS 2000 – EPSG 4674), comprising 36 rural properties (fazendas) held by approximately 24 landowners and entities. As an Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) project under VM0007 v1.8, the project prevents the legally authorized conversion of 20% of each property's area (approximately 14,957 ha total APD area) from dense ombrophilous forest to cattle pasture. Under the baseline scenario, landowners would legally convert these forest areas to cattle pasture in accordance with the Brazilian Forest Code, resulting in significant carbon emissions from forest clearing and land-use change. The project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá (pop. 20,136, IBGE 2022; IDHM 0.586), Parintins (pop. 96,251), and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The total estimated emission reductions and removals (ERRs) generated during the crediting period are 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e. The project crediting period spans 40 years, from 01 May 2023 to 30 April 2063. During this period, the average annual ERRs are estimated at 250,212.95 tCO₂e per year. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 34 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 Deforestation Dynamics Deforestation in the Brazilian Legal Amazon reached 5,796 km² in the August 2024–July 2025 PRODES/INPE cycle, representing an 11.08% decrease from the prior period and the third-lowest rate since measurements began in 1988. This marks the third consecutive year of decline under the Lula administration, with a cumulative 50% reduction compared to 2022. The state of Amazonas specifically recorded a 16.93% reduction in deforestation (to approximately 1,000 km²). However, forest degradation has increased significantly 2,500,000+ hectares degraded in 2024, a 163% increase compared to 2022, primarily due to fire. Despite declining national rates, private landowners in the Baixo Amazonas sub-region continue to exercise their legal right to convert up to 20% of property area under the Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). The Marcondes project addresses this ongoing baseline threat on 36 specific properties where deforestation authorization has been sought from IPAAM. Nhamundá municipality (14,107.5 km², pop. 20,136, IBGE 2022; pop. estimated 21,251 in 2025; IDHM 0.586) has 62 rural communities and limited economic alternatives to livestock, reinforcing the economic rationale for planned forest conversion. 2.1.15 Social Parameters (VCS, 3.18; CCB, G1.3) Socioeconomic conditions in the three municipalities hosting project properties are characterized by low human development indices, dependence on subsistence agriculture and extractivism, limited public services, and geographic isolation typical of the interior Amazon. Municipality Overview - Nhamundá Nhamundá: Population 20,136 (IBGE Census 2022), estimated at 21,251 (2025). Area: 14,107 km². Density: 1.43 inhabitants/km². IDHM: 0.586 (PNUD/IBGE, 2010) — classified as low human development. PIB per capita: R$11,905.57 (2023). School enrollment (6–14 years): 98.93%. Infant mortality: 13.25 per 1,000 live births (2023). The municipality has 57 identified communities, with the majority of the rural population (approximately 60%) living in dispersed riverine settlements along the Amazon and Nhamundá rivers. The economy is based on subsistence agriculture (manioc, rice, beans), fishing, livestock (small-scale), and extractivism (Brazil nuts, açaí, timber). Indigenous peoples present in the municipality include the Waiwái, Hixkaryana, and Karafáwyna. Access to the municipal seat is by river only, from Parintins (approximately 8 hours by boat). Health infrastructure comprises basic public facilities only, with referral cases transferred to Parintins or Manaus. Municipality Overview - Parintins Parintins: Population 96,372 (IBGE Census 2022), estimated at 101,855 (2025). Area: 5,956 km². Density: 16.18 inhabitants/km². IDHM: 0.658 (PNUD/IBGE, 2010) classified as medium human development. PIB per capita: R$17,193.26 (2023). Parintins is the regional center (Centro Sub-regional B) for the Baixo Amazonas region, serving as the commercial, educational, and healthcare hub for surrounding municipalities including Nhamundá and Barreirinha. The city is internationally known for the Festival Folclórico de Parintins (Boi-Bumbá Garantido vs. Caprichoso), a major cultural event. Two project properties (Mayara and André Marcondes IV) are located within Parintins municipality. Urban population share is approximately 68%.

The project area lies within the Middle Amazon basin, in the Nhamundá River watershed, a region of significant ecological value facing persistent deforestation pressures. According to Global Forest Watch (2020), Nhamundá municipality retains approximately 1.26 million hectares of natural forest, covering roughly 89% of its land area. Despite recent national progress, PRODES/INPE data shows Amazon deforestation declined by 50% cumulatively between 2022 and 2025, reaching 5,796 km² in the August 2024– July 2025 period the state of Amazonas remains the second-largest contributor to absolute deforestation in the Legal Amazon, with 1,016 km² cleared in the most recent PRODES cycle. The main drivers of deforestation in the project region include legal land clearance for cattle ranching and agriculture, selective and illegal logging, and pressure from infrastructure development and land speculation along river corridors. The Marcondes REDD+ project aims to avoid planned deforestation and degradation across a total project area of approximately 74,783 hectares (per GIS measurement, SIRGAS 2000 – EPSG 4674), comprising 36 rural properties (fazendas) held by approximately 24 landowners and entities. As an Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) project under VM0007 v1.8, the project prevents the legally authorized conversion of 20% of each property's area (approximately 14,957 ha total APD area) from dense ombrophilous forest to cattle pasture. Under the baseline scenario, landowners would legally convert these forest areas to cattle pasture in accordance with the Brazilian Forest Code, resulting in significant carbon emissions from forest clearing and land-use change. The project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá (pop. 20,136, IBGE 2022; IDHM 0.586), Parintins (pop. 96,251), and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The total estimated emission reductions and removals (ERRs) generated during the crediting period are 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 4 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 1 SUMMARY OF PROJECT BENEFITS The Marcondes Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) Project is an AFOLU initiative focused on Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), spanning a total area of 74,783 hectares of Amazon rainforest across 36 rural properties in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project's core objective is to conserve approximately 14,957 hectares of dense ombrophilous forest that would otherwise be legally converted to cattle pasture under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). By the end of the 40-year crediting period, an estimated 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of net GHG emission reductions will be achieved. This project is developed in alignment with the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity (CCB) Standards v3.1, ensuring measurable benefits across three critical areas. From a climate perspective, the conservation of 74,783 hectares of standing forest maintains critical carbon stocks (668.42 tCO₂e/ha) and preserves the hydrological functions of the Nhamundá River basin, a clearwater tributary draining the southern Guiana Shield. For local communities, the project delivers transformative benefits to the Comunidade Tradicional São Tomé do Mocambo do Arari (~80 families, Parintins) through a formal Benefit- Sharing Plan encompassing direct monetary benefits (participation in carbon credit revenue), community infrastructure (sanitation, energy, communication), training and capacity building, participatory forest monitoring with paid community guards, and cultural heritage support for traditional artisanal ceramics. The 40%/60% benefit-sharing structure ensures 60% of carbon revenues flow directly to the 36 participating landowners. The project prioritizes biodiversity conservation within the Uatumã–Trombetas Moist Forests ecoregion, harboring at least 10 globally threatened mammal species (including Inia geoffrensis — EN, Pteronura brasiliensis — EN, Tapirus terrestris — VU), 250+ bird species, 300+ fish species (including endemic taxa in the Nhamundá River), and threatened tree species (Swietenia macrophylla — VU, Bertholletia excelsa — VU). Forest conservation preserves ecosystem functions including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, watershed protection, and ecological connectivity. 1.1 Unique Project Benefits Outcome or impact estimated by the end of project lifetime Section referenc e 1) Avoiding the emission of 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of GHG, contributing to climate change mitigation over a 40-year period. 2.1.13 & 3

CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 10 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 2 PROJECT DETAILS 2.1 Project Goals, Design and Long-Term Viability 2.1.1 Summary Description of the Project (VCS, 3.2, 3.6, 3.10, 3.11, 3.13, 3.14; CCB, G1.2) The Marcondes REDD+ project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The project area lies within the Middle Amazon basin, in the Nhamundá River watershed, a region of significant ecological value facing persistent deforestation pressures. According to Global Forest Watch (2020), Nhamundá municipality retains approximately 1.26 million hectares of natural forest, covering roughly 89% of its land area. Despite recent national progress, PRODES/INPE data shows Amazon deforestation declined by 50% cumulatively between 2022 and 2025, reaching 5,796 km² in the August 2024– July 2025 period the state of Amazonas remains the second-largest contributor to absolute deforestation in the Legal Amazon, with 1,016 km² cleared in the most recent PRODES cycle. The main drivers of deforestation in the project region include legal land clearance for cattle ranching and agriculture, selective and illegal logging, and pressure from infrastructure development and land speculation along river corridors. The Marcondes REDD+ project aims to avoid planned deforestation and degradation across a total project area of approximately 74,783 hectares (per GIS measurement, SIRGAS 2000 – EPSG 4674), comprising 36 rural properties (fazendas) held by approximately 24 landowners and entities. As an Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) project under VM0007 v1.8, the project prevents the legally authorized conversion of 20% of each property's area (approximately 14,957 ha total APD area) from dense ombrophilous forest to cattle pasture. Under the baseline scenario, landowners would legally convert these forest areas to cattle pasture in accordance with the Brazilian Forest Code, resulting in significant carbon emissions from forest clearing and land-use change. The project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá (pop. 20,136, IBGE 2022; IDHM 0.586), Parintins (pop. 96,251), and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The total estimated emission reductions and removals (ERRs) generated during the crediting period are 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e. The project crediting period spans 40 years, from 01 May 2023 to 30 April 2063. During this period, the average annual ERRs are estimated at 250,212.95 tCO₂e per year. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 10 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 2 PROJECT DETAILS 2.1 Project Goals, Design and Long-Term Viability 2.1.1 Summary Description of the Project (VCS, 3.2, 3.6, 3.10, 3.11, 3.13, 3.14; CCB, G1.2) The Marcondes REDD+ project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The project area lies within the Middle Amazon basin, in the Nhamundá River watershed, a region of significant ecological value facing persistent deforestation pressures. According to Global Forest Watch (2020), Nhamundá municipality retains approximately 1.26 million hectares of natural forest, covering roughly 89% of its land area. Despite recent national progress, PRODES/INPE data shows Amazon deforestation declined by 50% cumulatively between 2022 and 2025, reaching 5,796 km² in the August 2024– July 2025 period the state of Amazonas remains the second-largest contributor to absolute deforestation in the Legal Amazon, with 1,016 km² cleared in the most recent PRODES cycle. The main drivers of deforestation in the project region include legal land clearance for cattle ranching and agriculture, selective and illegal logging, and pressure from infrastructure development and land speculation along river corridors. The Marcondes REDD+ project aims to avoid planned deforestation and degradation across a total project area of approximately 74,783 hectares (per GIS measurement, SIRGAS 2000 – EPSG 4674), comprising 36 rural properties (fazendas) held by approximately 24 landowners and entities. As an Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) project under VM0007 v1.8, the project prevents the legally authorized conversion of 20% of each property's area (approximately 14,957 ha total APD area) from dense ombrophilous forest to cattle pasture. Under the baseline scenario, landowners would legally convert these forest areas to cattle pasture in accordance with the Brazilian Forest Code, resulting in significant carbon emissions from forest clearing and land-use change. The project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá (pop. 20,136, IBGE 2022; IDHM 0.586), Parintins (pop. 96,251), and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. Under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law No. 12.651/2012), rural properties in the Legal Amazon must maintain an 80% Legal Reserve, meaning up to 20% may be legally converted. SCENARIO 3: Illegal deforestation exceeding 20% Illegal deforestation of over 20% of the property (deforestation without a grant), where the conversion of land use exceeds the legal limit, driven by pasture expansion, agricultural purposes, or real estate speculation. Evidence of deforestation drivers in the project area includes: (a) all 36 property owners hold environmental license applications (ASV) filed with IPAAM, demonstrating documented intent to clear the legally convertible 20% of their properties for pasture establishment; (b) PRODES/INPE and MapBiomas historical data show progressive deforestation on comparable private properties in the Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha municipalities; (c) the Nhamundá municipal economy is dominated by cattle ranching and subsistence agriculture (IBGE Municipal Agricultural Production data), with limited economic alternatives; (d) pasture land/agriculture land values exceed forest land values in the region, providing direct economic incentive for conversion; (e) road access improvements and population growth (4.82% increase from 2022 to 2024 per IBGE) are increasing pressure on forested lands. 2.2.2 Most-Likely Scenario Justification (CCB, G2.1) The most likely scenario observed for the Marcondes project area is the conversion of land use and land cover from forest to livestock areas, legally (APD). Legal deforestation of 20% of the property (Scenario 2) is considered the most plausible baseline scenario because the land is expected to be converted to non-forest land and the conversion is legally authorized and documented, following VM0007 v1.8. The identified deforestation agents are the landowners themselves, who have documented legal authorization to clear up to 20% of their property areas under the Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). Evidence includes: (a) IPAAM environmental license applications (ASV) filed by all 36 property holders; (b) property registration in SIGEF demonstrating legal control of the land; (c) CAR (Cadastro Ambiental Rural) registration identifying the legal reserve and APD-eligible areas; (d) economic profile consistent with agricultural expansion the landowners include individual farmers, family groups (e.g., Fazenda AnaLina I/II/III, Fazenda Irmãos Marcondes, Fazenda André Marcondes IV/V), and corporate entities (FIEMU Corporation, Marcondes Q Corporation) whose primary economic activity is or would be cattle ranching. 2.2.3 Community and Biodiversity Additionality (CCB, G2.2) In the absence of the Marcondes REDD+ project, neither the community benefits nor the biodiversity conservation outcomes would occur. The project area is located in a region of the

Without the project, these drivers would continue to advance, resulting in large-scale forest loss, degradation of ecosystems, and a decline in ecosystem services that sustain local communities. No government program, private organization, or community initiative currently possesses the financial, technical, or institutional capacity to prevent this deforestation or to generate the significant social and environmental benefits that the project will deliver. Although Brazilian environmental legislation primarily the Forest Code establishes requirements for Legal Reserves and Areas of Permanent Preservation, enforcement in remote Amazonian regions is limited. Environmental agencies such as IBAMA, ICMBio, and state-level authorities operate with insufficient personnel, financial resources, and field presence to monitor land-use change effectively. As a result, illegal deforestation persists, and legally authorized clearing continues unchecked. The project activities would not occur without carbon finance due to substantial financial barriers. Local communities lack the investment capacity needed to install renewable energy systems, develop potable water infrastructure, or establish agro-industries for processing NTFPs. Landowners similarly lack resources to implement forest monitoring systems, engage professional biodiversity technicians, or conduct long-term conservation planning. No government or donor program is currently committed to filling these gaps. Significant technological and knowledge barriers also prevent the implementation of sustainable development actions in the without-project scenario. Community members do not have access to the technical expertise required to manage NTFP value chains, apply sustainable harvesting techniques, conduct biodiversity monitoring, or maintain renewable energy systems. 2.2.4 Benefits to be used as Offsets (CCB, G2.2) The community and biodiversity benefits are not intended to be used as offsets but are documented and monitored under the CCB Standard to demonstrate the project's net positive impacts on local communities and ecosystems. 2.3 Safeguards and Stakeholder Engagement 2.3.1 Stakeholder Identification (VCS, 3.18, 3.19; CCB G1.5) The stakeholder identification process for the Marcondes REDD+ project was conducted using a structured, two-phase assessment, combining remote analysis and on-the-ground field validation. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 4 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 1 SUMMARY OF PROJECT BENEFITS The Marcondes Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) Project is an AFOLU initiative focused on Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), spanning a total area of 74,783 hectares of Amazon rainforest across 36 rural properties in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project's core objective is to conserve approximately 14,957 hectares of dense ombrophilous forest that would otherwise be legally converted to cattle pasture under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). By the end of the 40-year crediting period, an estimated 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of net GHG emission reductions will be achieved. This project is developed in alignment with the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity (CCB) Standards v3.1, ensuring measurable benefits across three critical areas. From a climate perspective, the conservation of 74,783 hectares of standing forest maintains critical carbon stocks (668.42 tCO₂e/ha) and preserves the hydrological functions of the Nhamundá River basin, a clearwater tributary draining the southern Guiana Shield. For local communities, the project delivers transformative benefits to the Comunidade Tradicional São Tomé do Mocambo do Arari (~80 families, Parintins) through a formal Benefit- Sharing Plan encompassing direct monetary benefits (participation in carbon credit revenue), community infrastructure (sanitation, energy, communication), training and capacity building, participatory forest monitoring with paid community guards, and cultural heritage support for traditional artisanal ceramics. The 40%/60% benefit-sharing structure ensures 60% of carbon revenues flow directly to the 36 participating landowners. The project prioritizes biodiversity conservation within the Uatumã–Trombetas Moist Forests ecoregion, harboring at least 10 globally threatened mammal species (including Inia geoffrensis — EN, Pteronura brasiliensis — EN, Tapirus terrestris — VU), 250+ bird species, 300+ fish species (including endemic taxa in the Nhamundá River), and threatened tree species (Swietenia macrophylla — VU, Bertholletia excelsa — VU). Forest conservation preserves ecosystem functions including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, watershed protection, and ecological connectivity. 1.1 Unique Project Benefits Outcome or impact estimated by the end of project lifetime Section referenc e 1) Avoiding the emission of 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of GHG, contributing to climate change mitigation over a 40-year period. 2.1.13 & 3

CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 4 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 1 SUMMARY OF PROJECT BENEFITS The Marcondes Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) Project is an AFOLU initiative focused on Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), spanning a total area of 74,783 hectares of Amazon rainforest across 36 rural properties in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project's core objective is to conserve approximately 14,957 hectares of dense ombrophilous forest that would otherwise be legally converted to cattle pasture under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). By the end of the 40-year crediting period, an estimated 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of net GHG emission reductions will be achieved. This project is developed in alignment with the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity (CCB) Standards v3.1, ensuring measurable benefits across three critical areas. From a climate perspective, the conservation of 74,783 hectares of standing forest maintains critical carbon stocks (668.42 tCO₂e/ha) and preserves the hydrological functions of the Nhamundá River basin, a clearwater tributary draining the southern Guiana Shield. For local communities, the project delivers transformative benefits to the Comunidade Tradicional São Tomé do Mocambo do Arari (~80 families, Parintins) through a formal Benefit- Sharing Plan encompassing direct monetary benefits (participation in carbon credit revenue), community infrastructure (sanitation, energy, communication), training and capacity building, participatory forest monitoring with paid community guards, and cultural heritage support for traditional artisanal ceramics. The 40%/60% benefit-sharing structure ensures 60% of carbon revenues flow directly to the 36 participating landowners. The project prioritizes biodiversity conservation within the Uatumã–Trombetas Moist Forests ecoregion, harboring at least 10 globally threatened mammal species (including Inia geoffrensis — EN, Pteronura brasiliensis — EN, Tapirus terrestris — VU), 250+ bird species, 300+ fish species (including endemic taxa in the Nhamundá River), and threatened tree species (Swietenia macrophylla — VU, Bertholletia excelsa — VU). Forest conservation preserves ecosystem functions including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, watershed protection, and ecological connectivity. 1.1 Unique Project Benefits Outcome or impact estimated by the end of project lifetime Section referenc e 1) Avoiding the emission of 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of GHG, contributing to climate change mitigation over a 40-year period. 2.1.13 & 3

CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 4 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 1 SUMMARY OF PROJECT BENEFITS The Marcondes Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) Project is an AFOLU initiative focused on Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), spanning a total area of 74,783 hectares of Amazon rainforest across 36 rural properties in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project's core objective is to conserve approximately 14,957 hectares of dense ombrophilous forest that would otherwise be legally converted to cattle pasture under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). By the end of the 40-year crediting period, an estimated 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of net GHG emission reductions will be achieved. This project is developed in alignment with the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity (CCB) Standards v3.1, ensuring measurable benefits across three critical areas. From a climate perspective, the conservation of 74,783 hectares of standing forest maintains critical carbon stocks (668.42 tCO₂e/ha) and preserves the hydrological functions of the Nhamundá River basin, a clearwater tributary draining the southern Guiana Shield. For local communities, the project delivers transformative benefits to the Comunidade Tradicional São Tomé do Mocambo do Arari (~80 families, Parintins) through a formal Benefit- Sharing Plan encompassing direct monetary benefits (participation in carbon credit revenue), community infrastructure (sanitation, energy, communication), training and capacity building, participatory forest monitoring with paid community guards, and cultural heritage support for traditional artisanal ceramics. The 40%/60% benefit-sharing structure ensures 60% of carbon revenues flow directly to the 36 participating landowners. The project prioritizes biodiversity conservation within the Uatumã–Trombetas Moist Forests ecoregion, harboring at least 10 globally threatened mammal species (including Inia geoffrensis — EN, Pteronura brasiliensis — EN, Tapirus terrestris — VU), 250+ bird species, 300+ fish species (including endemic taxa in the Nhamundá River), and threatened tree species (Swietenia macrophylla — VU, Bertholletia excelsa — VU). Forest conservation preserves ecosystem functions including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, watershed protection, and ecological connectivity. 1.1 Unique Project Benefits Outcome or impact estimated by the end of project lifetime Section referenc e 1) Avoiding the emission of 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of GHG, contributing to climate change mitigation over a 40-year period. 2.1.13 & 3

CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 10 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 2 PROJECT DETAILS 2.1 Project Goals, Design and Long-Term Viability 2.1.1 Summary Description of the Project (VCS, 3.2, 3.6, 3.10, 3.11, 3.13, 3.14; CCB, G1.2) The Marcondes REDD+ project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The project area lies within the Middle Amazon basin, in the Nhamundá River watershed, a region of significant ecological value facing persistent deforestation pressures. According to Global Forest Watch (2020), Nhamundá municipality retains approximately 1.26 million hectares of natural forest, covering roughly 89% of its land area. Despite recent national progress, PRODES/INPE data shows Amazon deforestation declined by 50% cumulatively between 2022 and 2025, reaching 5,796 km² in the August 2024– July 2025 period the state of Amazonas remains the second-largest contributor to absolute deforestation in the Legal Amazon, with 1,016 km² cleared in the most recent PRODES cycle. The main drivers of deforestation in the project region include legal land clearance for cattle ranching and agriculture, selective and illegal logging, and pressure from infrastructure development and land speculation along river corridors. The Marcondes REDD+ project aims to avoid planned deforestation and degradation across a total project area of approximately 74,783 hectares (per GIS measurement, SIRGAS 2000 – EPSG 4674), comprising 36 rural properties (fazendas) held by approximately 24 landowners and entities. As an Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) project under VM0007 v1.8, the project prevents the legally authorized conversion of 20% of each property's area (approximately 14,957 ha total APD area) from dense ombrophilous forest to cattle pasture. Under the baseline scenario, landowners would legally convert these forest areas to cattle pasture in accordance with the Brazilian Forest Code, resulting in significant carbon emissions from forest clearing and land-use change. The project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá (pop. 20,136, IBGE 2022; IDHM 0.586), Parintins (pop. 96,251), and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The total estimated emission reductions and removals (ERRs) generated during the crediting period are 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e. The project crediting period spans 40 years, from 01 May 2023 to 30 April 2063. During this period, the average annual ERRs are estimated at 250,212.95 tCO₂e per year. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 42 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 SCENARIO 2: Legal deforestation of 20% of the property (APD) Legal deforestation of 20% of the property (deforestation with allowances), where land use conversion is allowed by law, i.e., forest suppression for pasture (livestock). Under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law No. 12.651/2012), rural properties in the Legal Amazon must maintain an 80% Legal Reserve, meaning up to 20% may be legally converted. SCENARIO 3: Illegal deforestation exceeding 20% Illegal deforestation of over 20% of the property (deforestation without a grant), where the conversion of land use exceeds the legal limit, driven by pasture expansion, agricultural purposes, or real estate speculation. Evidence of deforestation drivers in the project area includes: (a) all 36 property owners hold environmental license applications (ASV) filed with IPAAM, demonstrating documented intent to clear the legally convertible 20% of their properties for pasture establishment; (b) PRODES/INPE and MapBiomas historical data show progressive deforestation on comparable private properties in the Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha municipalities; (c) the Nhamundá municipal economy is dominated by cattle ranching and subsistence agriculture (IBGE Municipal Agricultural Production data), with limited economic alternatives; (d) pasture land/agriculture land values exceed forest land values in the region, providing direct economic incentive for conversion; (e) road access improvements and population growth (4.82% increase from 2022 to 2024 per IBGE) are increasing pressure on forested lands. 2.2.2 Most-Likely Scenario Justification (CCB, G2.1) The most likely scenario observed for the Marcondes project area is the conversion of land use and land cover from forest to livestock areas, legally (APD). Legal deforestation of 20% of the property (Scenario 2) is considered the most plausible baseline scenario because the land is expected to be converted to non-forest land and the conversion is legally authorized and documented, following VM0007 v1.8. The identified deforestation agents are the landowners themselves, who have documented legal authorization to clear up to 20% of their property areas under the Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). Evidence includes: (a) IPAAM environmental license applications (ASV) filed by all 36 property holders; (b) property registration in SIGEF demonstrating legal control of the land; (c) CAR (Cadastro Ambiental Rural) registration identifying the legal reserve and APD-eligible areas; (d) economic profile consistent with agricultural expansion the landowners include individual farmers, family groups (e.g., Fazenda AnaLina I/II/III, Fazenda Irmãos Marcondes, Fazenda André Marcondes IV/V), and corporate entities (FIEMU Corporation, Marcondes Q Corporation) whose primary economic activity is or would be cattle ranching. 2.2.3 Community and Biodiversity Additionality (CCB, G2.2) In the absence of the Marcondes REDD+ project, neither the community benefits nor the biodiversity conservation outcomes would occur. The project area is located in a region of the

CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 43 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 eastern Amazon where planned deforestation is legally permissible and widely practiced due to expanding pressures from cattle ranching, agriculture, timber extraction, and other land-use conversion activities. Without the project, these drivers would continue to advance, resulting in large-scale forest loss, degradation of ecosystems, and a decline in ecosystem services that sustain local communities. No government program, private organization, or community initiative currently possesses the financial, technical, or institutional capacity to prevent this deforestation or to generate the significant social and environmental benefits that the project will deliver. Although Brazilian environmental legislation primarily the Forest Code establishes requirements for Legal Reserves and Areas of Permanent Preservation, enforcement in remote Amazonian regions is limited. Environmental agencies such as IBAMA, ICMBio, and state-level authorities operate with insufficient personnel, financial resources, and field presence to monitor land-use change effectively. As a result, illegal deforestation persists, and legally authorized clearing continues unchecked. The project activities would not occur without carbon finance due to substantial financial barriers. Local communities lack the investment capacity needed to install renewable energy systems, develop potable water infrastructure, or establish agro-industries for processing NTFPs. Landowners similarly lack resources to implement forest monitoring systems, engage professional biodiversity technicians, or conduct long-term conservation planning. No government or donor program is currently committed to filling these gaps. Significant technological and knowledge barriers also prevent the implementation of sustainable development actions in the without-project scenario. Community members do not have access to the technical expertise required to manage NTFP value chains, apply sustainable harvesting techniques, conduct biodiversity monitoring, or maintain renewable energy systems. 2.2.4 Benefits to be used as Offsets (CCB, G2.2) The community and biodiversity benefits are not intended to be used as offsets but are documented and monitored under the CCB Standard to demonstrate the project's net positive impacts on local communities and ecosystems. 2.3 Safeguards and Stakeholder Engagement 2.3.1 Stakeholder Identification (VCS, 3.18, 3.19; CCB G1.5) The stakeholder identification process for the Marcondes REDD+ project was conducted using a structured, two-phase assessment, combining remote analysis and on-the-ground field validation. Stakeholders were identified based on their legal rights, forest resource dependence, potential influence on project outcomes, and possession of relevant local knowledge. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 22 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 Land ownership and tenure of the Marcondes REDD+ project properties are governed by applicable federal and state legislation in Brazil, which establishes the legal basis for possession, environmental registration, georeferenced boundary certification, and formal land tenure rights. Federal Legislation ▪ Brazilian Civil Code (Law No. 10.406/2002, Articles 1.196–1.228): Recognizes possession (posse) as a protected right and establishes usucapião as a legal pathway to ownership. ▪ Brazilian Forest Code (Law No. 12.651/2012): Establishes the requirement for Cadastro Ambiental Rural (CAR) registration and mandates an 80% Legal Reserve for rural properties located in the Legal Amazon. ▪ Law No. 10.267/2001 and Decree No. 4.449/2002: Establish the SIGEF system (Sistema de Gestão Fundiária) and define requirements for georeferenced rural property registration. ▪ Law No. 6.015/1973 (Public Registries Law): Regulates property registration and the Matrícula system at the Cartório de Registro de Imóveis. State Legislation (Amazonas) ▪ State Law No. 2.665/2001: Regulates state land policy, including the issuance of Concessão de Direito Real de Uso (CDRU) for state lands and terras devolutas. ▪ State Law No. 3.135/2007: Establishes the Amazonas State Policy on Climate Change, providing the legal framework for carbon credit projects and ecosystem services. Land Ownership The Marcondes REDD+ project is a grouped project and for validation comprises 36 rural properties located primarily in the municipality of Nhamundá, Parintins and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The total project area is approximately 74,698 hectares, held by approximately 24 landowners and legal entities. All 36 project properties are registered in the SIGEF system (Sistema de Gestão Fundiária) managed by INCRA, providing legally recognized, georeferenced, non-overlapping property boundaries. All properties are also registered in the Cadastro Ambiental Rural (CAR), which includes declared georeferenced boundaries, identification of Permanent Protection Areas (APPs), and demarcation of Legal Reserves in accordance with the 80% requirement applicable in the Legal Amazon. Applications for Concessão de Direito Real de Uso (CDRU) have been submitted to the SECT (Secretaria de Estado das Cidades e Territórios) for all properties, providing secure long-term rights of land use and management. Environmental license applications (Autorização de Supressão Vegetal — ASV) have been filed with IPAAM (Instituto de Proteção Ambiental do Amazonas) for all properties, confirming the legal authorization for land conversion that constitutes the basis for the APD baseline scenario. CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 29 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 Figure: General Location of the Project Geology, Geomorphology and Topography The project area is situated within the Amazon Sedimentary Basin, underlain by Cretaceous and Tertiary sedimentary formations. The predominant geological unit is the Alter do Chão Formation (Cretaceous–Paleogene), composed of sandstones, siltstones, and claystones, typical of the central Amazon lowlands. Geomorphologically, the landscape comprises dissected tertiary plateaus (terra firme), fluvial terraces, and extensive floodplain systems (várzea) along the Amazon and Nhamundá rivers. Topography is gently undulating to flat, with elevations generally between 30 m and 120 m in the terra firme zones. The Nhamundá River, which forms the boundary between the states of Amazonas and Pará, has a sandy bed and clear waters, with several rapids in its upper course and lake formations at the confluence with the Paracatu River.

CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 65 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 VMD0011 v1.2 This module is applicable for calculating market-effects leakage from projects that are anticipated to reduce levels of wood harvest substantially and permanently. When project activities result in reductions in wood harvest, it is likely that production could shift to other areas of the country to compensate for the reduction, including activity shifting to forested peatland that is drained as a consequence of project implementation. This tool shall be used in countries where wood harvest happens on forested peatland regardless of the absence of peatland within the project boundary. As referenced in the Framework (REDD MF), the module is mandatory where: The deforestation process involves harvesting timber for commercial markets. Baseline is calculated using BL-DFW and firewood or charcoal is harvested for commercial markets. In all other circumstances, the module should not be used. The module is mandatory when the deforestation process involves the extraction of timber for commercial markets. The module is applicable to the Marcondes Project as project activities are expected to substantially reduce and prevent wood harvesting within the project boundary through the protection and conservation of native forest areas. Such reductions in timber supply could potentially lead to market-effects leakage if wood production shifts to other regions within Brazil to meet market demand. The project therefore assesses the potential for market-effects leakage. VMD0013 v1.3 This module is applicable to REDD project activities with emissions from biomass burning and REDD-WRC project activities with emissions from biomass and/or peat burning. This module is also applicable to RWE and ARR-RWE project activities with emissions from peat burning. In the baseline scenario, fire is used to clear land, resulting in emissions of CO2, N2O and CH4. When used in the baseline, accounting must occur both under the baseline and in the project scenario and both in the project area and in the leakage belt. Where fires occur ex- post in areas that coincide with deforested or degraded areas in the baseline, the module should be used to account for greenhouse gas emissions. VMD0016 v1.3 This module provides guidance on how to stratify the project area into discrete, relatively homogeneous units to improve the accuracy and precision of Strata are only used for forest classes under deforestation pressure and are the same in the case of the baseline and project scenario.

Project Crediting Period and Registration Timelines 3.8.1 The initial crediting period start date shall: 1) be consistent with the definition of initial crediting period start date in the VCS Program Definitions. 2) conform to any criteria set out in the applied methodology. 3) be established based on implementation of the earliest project activity, where the project includes multiple project activities. 4) determine the start of the first project monitoring period, which shall begin on the initial crediting period start date. Some methodologies may require project proponents to quantify emissions that occur prior to this date to account for all project or baseline emissions. The initial crediting period start date for the Marcondes REDD+ Project is 01 May 2023, which is consistent with the definition of the initial crediting period start date under the VCS Program and conforms to the criteria specified in the applied methodology. The project does not involve multiple project activities and implements a single REDD+ activity in a grouped project design aimed at avoiding planned deforestation (APD). Accordingly, the crediting period start date is established based on the earliest implementation of project activities undertaken to prevent planned deforestation. The selected date corresponds to the commencement of project implementation activities, including the execution of carbon credit agreements with participating landowners and the initiation of monitoring activities across properties located in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha in the state of Amazonas. This date also determines the start of the first monitoring period, from which emission reductions are accounted for under the project. The applied methodology does not require quantification of emissions occurring prior to the crediting period start date; therefore, this provision is not applicable to the project. results.bestEvidenceQuote: CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 41 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 Permanence Mechanisms: ▪ 100-year longevity commitment in all carbon credit agreements ▪ VCS Standard v5.0, Section 3.2.19 provisions for instance exits ▪ AFOLU Non-Permanence Risk buffer pool ▪ Integration of sustainable economic activities (NTFP value chains, agroforestry) creating lasting conservation incentives 2.1.22 Financial Sustainability (CCB, G1.12) Financing of project activities is guaranteed by funds committed by the project proponents from the project start date until the first verification. The financing structure for the Marcondes REDD+ project is based on carbon credit revenues under the VCS Program, supplemented by initial investment from the project proponent: The Project Proponent has secured project financing through carbon credit offtaker agreements that provide advance funding for project implementation. A portion of the forecasted carbon credits has been committed under forward purchase agreements, ensuring financial resources are available from the project start date through the first verification cycle. This pre-financing covers monitoring infrastructure, community program implementation, and project development costs. Ongoing project financing is sustained through the sale of verified carbon credits (VCUs) on the voluntary carbon market, with revenues allocated according to the benefit-sharing structure defined in the carbon credit agreements with landowners. A portion of carbon credit revenues is dedicated to the community benefit fund, administered in consultation with the Comunidade São Tomé do Mocambo, ensuring long-term financial sustainability of community programs and biodiversity conservation activities. 2.2 Without-project Land Use Scenario and Additionality 2.2.1 Conditions Prior to Project Initiation and Land Use Scenarios without the Project (VCS, 3.13; CCB, G2.1) The following scenarios represent the range of possible land-use outcomes in the absence of the Marcondes REDD+ project. These scenarios were developed based on analysis of regional land- use dynamics, landowner intentions, legal frameworks, and historical deforestation patterns in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The landowner remains responsible for taxes to maintain ownership.

CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 43 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 eastern Amazon where planned deforestation is legally permissible and widely practiced due to expanding pressures from cattle ranching, agriculture, timber extraction, and other land-use conversion activities. Without the project, these drivers would continue to advance, resulting in large-scale forest loss, degradation of ecosystems, and a decline in ecosystem services that sustain local communities. No government program, private organization, or community initiative currently possesses the financial, technical, or institutional capacity to prevent this deforestation or to generate the significant social and environmental benefits that the project will deliver. Although Brazilian environmental legislation primarily the Forest Code establishes requirements for Legal Reserves and Areas of Permanent Preservation, enforcement in remote Amazonian regions is limited. Environmental agencies such as IBAMA, ICMBio, and state-level authorities operate with insufficient personnel, financial resources, and field presence to monitor land-use change effectively. As a result, illegal deforestation persists, and legally authorized clearing continues unchecked. The project activities would not occur without carbon finance due to substantial financial barriers. Local communities lack the investment capacity needed to install renewable energy systems, develop potable water infrastructure, or establish agro-industries for processing NTFPs. Landowners similarly lack resources to implement forest monitoring systems, engage professional biodiversity technicians, or conduct long-term conservation planning. No government or donor program is currently committed to filling these gaps. Significant technological and knowledge barriers also prevent the implementation of sustainable development actions in the without-project scenario. Community members do not have access to the technical expertise required to manage NTFP value chains, apply sustainable harvesting techniques, conduct biodiversity monitoring, or maintain renewable energy systems. 2.2.4 Benefits to be used as Offsets (CCB, G2.2) The community and biodiversity benefits are not intended to be used as offsets but are documented and monitored under the CCB Standard to demonstrate the project's net positive impacts on local communities and ecosystems. 2.3 Safeguards and Stakeholder Engagement 2.3.1 Stakeholder Identification (VCS, 3.18, 3.19; CCB G1.5) The stakeholder identification process for the Marcondes REDD+ project was conducted using a structured, two-phase assessment, combining remote analysis and on-the-ground field validation. Stakeholders were identified based on their legal rights, forest resource dependence, potential influence on project outcomes, and possession of relevant local knowledge. Phase 1 — Remote Stakeholder Identification
